evidence: repro_D/d01_reactivating.py: one cell carrying only its IE productive marker via run_one() with the packaged catalogue -> EBV reactivating (intended); HHV-6A (U90 HUM_HERP6_HHV6_p24) reactivating; HHV-6B (U95) reactivating; HHV-7 (U90 gp81) reactivating; VZV (ORF62 gp63) reactivating; all with latency_not_observable=True; only HCMV -> indeterminate. The HCMV exclusion is a one-name allow-list; the same 'latency mimics IE expression' argument applies to VZV (ORF62/ORF63/ORF4 transcripts detected in latent ganglia: Cohrs 1996 J Virol 70:2789; Nagel 2011; contested by Depledge 2018 post-mortem RNA-seq finding only VLT) and HHV-6 (ciHHV-6 individuals express U90/IE1A most highly in GTEx; secondary source hhv-6foundation.org summary, primary paper unverified). For latency_observable=false viruses 'reactivating' is a presence-only call with no latency anchor, i.e. the non-specific call PROG-12 rejected for HCMV. docs/output_reference.md:463 says 'Never emitted for HCMV' only.
proposed_fix: Gate reactivating on latency_observable_in_rna (or add a per-virus reactivation_applicable catalogue column); at minimum add VZV/HHV-6A/6B/HHV-7 to REACTIVATION_NOT_APPLICABLE, report n_cells_reactivating=not_applicable, and document in the States table.

evidence: repro_D/d01_reactivating.py part 2: VZV index containing only ORF62 (4 of 5 catalogue markers unresolved): run_one logs WARNING 'calls use the reduced marker set' and still emits state=reactivating; summary n_cells_reactivating=1, caveat only '4 of 5 catalogue markers did not resolve'. reactivating = IE evidence AND absence of any later productive group; when the later markers are the unresolved ones, later_cols is empty and every IE-positive cell is reactivating (absence unobservable). Likewise productive>=min_breadth may be unreachable and latency_observable is a catalogue property, not an index property. PROG-14 'fail loudly' only warns; states are emitted as normal.
proposed_fix: In run_one, if no resolved non-IE productive marker exists force reactivating_applicable=False; if fewer than min_breadth productive groups resolved flag productive unreachable; add a summary column naming which classes were assessable on this index.

evidence: n_cells_reactivating is integer 0 (not 'not_applicable') for viruses with no productive immediate_early catalogue marker (HSV-1, HSV-2, KSHV): the state is structurally unreachable (catalogue: 0 IE productive rows for HHV1/HHV2/HHV8; KSHV ORF50/RTA absent) yet the summary reads as 'none observed'. latent/mixed get a documented by-construction flag; reactivating has none.
proposed_fix: Emit not_applicable (or a reactivating_observable column) when no productive IE marker resolved; document.

evidence: repro_D/d04_refstrategy_viralscan_schema.py part 1: a per_cell_viral.tsv with the real v3 columns (barcode, virus_name, viral_molecules_total_est, molecules_total_est, viral_fraction, is_called_cell) -> status='failed', 'per_cell_viral.tsv missing required columns'. The parser requires the pre-v3 column viral_umi (absent from detection.py since the schema rename; grep viral_umi src shows only reference_strategy.py), so every ViralScan row of the 12-row reference-strategy benchmark is 'failed' on real output. tests/test_reference_strategy_benchmark.py:218 builds its fixture with the legacy viral_umi column, so CI is green. Additionally per_cell_viral.tsv holds ONLY infected cells (detection.py:668 'only infected cells'), so anchor_barcodes=set(counts) is 'cells with viral reads', not called cells: denominator_method_called_cells and the intersected denominator_shared_anchor_cells are selected on the outcome and not comparable with STARsolo's filtered-barcode anchor (and is_called_cell is ignored).
proposed_fix: Read viral_molecules_total_est (accept viral_umi as legacy alias); take the anchor from is_called_cell==true (or called_cells.tsv); change the fixture to the v3 schema and add a test that feeds detection.build_per_cell output through the parser.

evidence: repro_D/d05_refstrategy_universe_delta.py (patching _row_metrics): when STARsolo-combined is incomplete the fixed barcode universe is built from the surviving combined rows only (ViralScan's infected cells = 2 barcodes), so the 'complete' STARsolo two_step row reports target_umi_fixed=10.0 over fixed=2 while it actually saw 15 UMI in 3 barcodes (barcode C silently dropped); no status/flag records that the universe was shrunk and validate_results only checks the denominator is the same across rows. Same run: combined_vs_two_step_delta is '0' for every combined row (the pair is never in the dict yet since combined precedes two_step in METHOD_ROWS, so the 'combined - two_step' branch at :1134-1138 is dead), and for two_step rows it is two_step - combined (sign opposite to the column name) and equals the whole target UMI (10.0) when the combined row failed (0 UMI treated as data).
proposed_fix: Fail (or mark 'incomplete: fixed universe from N of M combined rows') when any combined row is incomplete; compute delta symmetrically after all rows are known as combined - two_step, '' / NA when either side is incomplete; add a test with one failed combined row.

evidence: repro_D/d04_refstrategy_viralscan_schema.py part 2 against the shipped catalogue display names: HSV-1 target_regex matches 'Human herpesvirus 1' AND 'Macacine alphaherpesvirus 1' (herpesvirus[_ -]?1 has no (?![0-9]) guard and no 'human' anchor; the hhv-?1 guard added for HHV1 does not cover this alternative), so cercopithecine/macacine HV-1 (B virus) reads would be counted as HSV-1 target UMI in the benchmark; EBV off_target matches 'Macacine alphaherpesvirus 1' and 'Papiine betaherpesvirus 3' (non-human viruses) as 'related off-target'. Matching also runs over STARsolo features.tsv text (gene id + name), unchecked here.
proposed_fix: Anchor the HSV-1 alternatives with human[_ -]?(alpha)?herpesvirus[_ -]?1(?![0-9]) and use the identity table's virus_key rather than names where available; test the regexes against every catalogue display name (assert target and off-target sets are disjoint and species-correct).

evidence: repro_D/d06_refstrategy_presence_provenance.py: (1) a 8.6 MB plain GTF with the EBV gene in the middle (4.3 MB of other rows on both sides) -> _presence == 'not_detected_in_sample' (only the first and last 2 MB are scanned), so validate_audit_rows raises 'expected viruses absent' for a reference that contains them; conversely a regex hit in the head/tail of a combined host+virus file counts as present without checking the virus is a real feature. (2) _validate_provenance accepts bool counts (isinstance(True,int)) and accepts fetched+missing < expected (only '>' is rejected: expected=2021, fetched=5, missing=5 -> accepted), so an un-accounted anellovirus gap passes the 'provenance' gate.
proposed_fix: Stream the whole file for presence (it is a one-off audit) or build presence from the identity table; require fetched+missing == expected and reject bool.
